_what_this_is: One entry per closed optimisation loop on a noise experiment. A loop is measured, changed ONE thing, re-measured. An entry without both a before and an after number is not a loop and does not belong here. Read by coverage.py.

_fields.dataset: the dataset it was measured on, and how many molecules
_fields.changed: the one thing that changed, in words
_fields.before: the number before, with its unit named
_fields.after: the number after, with its unit named
_fields.kept: true if the change stayed in the file, false if it was reverted
_fields.note: optional: what the number does not settle

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 per training fold, saprot, random forest, spearman
loops.changed: the injected dose, from the level 0.5 n07 runs to level 2.0, at the same one molecule in ten corrupted
loops.before: the clean-to-corrupted gap a recovery divides by, 0.0192 spearman against a clean score of 0.5985 spearman
loops.after: the same gap, 0.1639 spearman against the same clean score of 0.5985 spearman
loops.note: Measured over 3 scaffold-grouped folds and 3 noise draws. NOT applied: the injected level is the owner's to set and it is the axis the experiment is about. It is recorded because at level 0.5 the completed run on disk, at 2 folds and 1 noise draw, measured that gap as NEGATIVE -- clean 0.5775 spearman against corrupted 0.5847 -- so every recovery in its hybrid block came back undefined. Level 1.0 gives 0.0656 spearman and level 3.0 gives 0.2758. Doubling the corrupted share from one molecule in ten to one in five moved the gap from 0.0192 to 0.0225 spearman at level 0.5 and from 0.1639 to 0.1643 at level 2.0, so the dose is what damages the model and the count of corrupted molecules barely is.

loops.dataset: synthetic, 90 rows, 70 per training fold — a cost measurement, not a score
loops.changed: the iteration harness's n11 cuts rebound onto the two lists the loops actually read, and the extra-target list gated at the place the targets are built
loops.before: 28 downstream model fits per estimator per estimation space with one downstream model, and one Gaussian-process out-of-fold pass per (fold, draw, space)
loops.after: 10 downstream model fits per estimator per estimation space with one downstream model, and no Gaussian-process out-of-fold pass
loops.note: This settles nothing about which estimator to pair with which correction. The harness had declared these cuts since 2026-09-18 and they reached nothing: it rebound ALPHAS, an alias bound once at import that the result file reports and no loop reads, while the loops read SMOOTH_ALPHAS and WEIGHT_STRENGTHS; and it rebound EXTRA_TARGETS, which run() wrote into the result file while building both targets by hand. So a run under the harness reported two cuts it had not made and paid for a Gaussian process it had asked to drop. n11 still produced no result file on 2026-09-20 — every result store it reads raises StaleResultDB for a missing distance_metric column.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 per training fold, saprot, random forest, spearman
loops.changed: how far a label moves toward its target, from the alpha of 0.5 that oof_smooth and gp_smooth run at to an alpha of 1.0, with the suspicion score rescaled the same way in both
loops.before: aiming at a Gaussian-process posterior mean, 0.4509 spearman; aiming at a LightGBM out-of-fold prediction, 0.4581 spearman; aiming at the mean label of the ten nearest molecules, 0.4331 spearman
loops.after: aiming at a Gaussian-process posterior mean, 0.4996 spearman; aiming at a LightGBM out-of-fold prediction, 0.4703 spearman; aiming at the mean label of the ten nearest molecules, 0.4552 spearman
loops.note: Three folds, one noise draw each, injected level 2.0, one molecule in ten given the wide error. Clean 0.5985 spearman, corrupted 0.4111, so the gap is 0.1874 spearman. The mean of three folds moves the right way for all three targets, but FOLD BY FOLD it is 7 of 9 paired readings, not 9: on the third fold moving the whole way LOST for the LightGBM target (0.4262 down to 0.3866 spearman) and for the neighbour mean (0.4076 down to 0.3951). Only the Gaussian-process target won on all three folds. The best single setting is gp_smooth moving the whole way, 0.4996 spearman and 47.2 percent of the gap, against 0.4509 and 21.2 percent at the half-way setting it runs at -- so the two model-based corrections coming last of seven in the completed run is the ranking of one alpha, not of the targets. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: for the neighbour-mean target, overwriting the flagged tenth outright scored 0.4829 spearman against 0.4552 for moving every label the whole way, so knn_smooth's shape is not beaten. And rescaling the suspicion score by its rank put the labels closest to clean on all three folds -- 7.12 to 7.69 label units against 10.85 to 12.95 for every other setting -- while recovering the least of the gap, so the correction that repairs the most labels is not the one that recovers the most score. NOT APPLIED: one dataset, one representation, one downstream model, one dose, and n18 already sweeps this same alpha over 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0 for exactly these two cleanups. WHY IT MOVES AT ALL: the Outlier condition is Huber contamination at lambda 3, so every training label carries an error and the flagged tenth carries one about three times wider -- 39.32 label units from clean on the 39 molecules flagged in fold 0 against 12.67 on the other 409, clean label standard deviation 10.12. Run cost 5999 seconds for the three folds on a machine at load 200 to 480.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, saprot, 3 scaffold-grouped folds, 1 corruption draw each, injected level 2.0, one molecule in ten corrupted
loops.changed: the fraction of the way a score-proportional correction moves a label, from 0.5 to 1.0, holding the correction's target fixed
loops.before: share of the 0.1874 spearman clean-to-corrupted gap recovered at 0.5: 21.2% for the gaussian-process target, 11.7% for the neighbour mean, 25.0% for the out-of-fold prediction
loops.after: at 1.0: 47.2%, 23.5% and 31.6% for the same three targets
loops.note: COMPLETE at 3 folds, 5999 seconds. Clean 0.5985 spearman against corrupted 0.4111. NOT applied: the correction strength is n18's axis to settle and n18 measured the opposite on real labels, so the default is not this loop's to move. Recorded because it refutes the reading that the min-max rescale was what held these corrections back. Replacing the raw score with its rank at the same 1.0, which makes that rescale the identity, LOST at all three targets: 19.4%, 9.4% and 13.3%. ⛔ CORRECTED 2026-09-21: this entry said both comparisons held at 3 of 3 targets on every one of the three passes. They do not. The partial tables the probe prints are CUMULATIVE means over the passes so far, not per-pass values, and reading them as per-pass is what produced that claim. Recovering each pass from the cumulative means: moving the whole way beat moving half way in 7 of 9 paired readings, losing on the third fold for the out-of-fold target (0.4262 down to 0.3866 spearman) and for the neighbour mean (0.4076 down to 0.3951). The raw score beat its rank in 8 of 9, losing on the second fold for the neighbour mean (0.4963 against 0.4881). Only the gaussian-process target won both comparisons on all three folds. The three-fold MEANS still move the way this entry reports. ⛔ DUPLICATE: this is the same measurement as the entry whose `changed` begins "how far a label moves toward its target"; one run, two rows, so the table counts it twice. The TARGET matters less than one pass suggested: the gaussian process leads at 47.2% but the neighbour mean's best shape is 'replace' at 38.3%, which read 11.0% after one pass and 26.2% after two, so that cell is not settled. Separately, the shape that moved labels closest to their clean values was not the shape that scored best -- rank at 1.0 cut the mean distance from a corrupted training label to its clean value from 14.94 label units to between 7.12 and 7.69 and still lost the held-out spearman to proportional at 1.0, which reached only 10.85 to 11.03 units. The gaussian process ran without importance-weighted kernel inputs. ⛔ n18 measured the SAME axis on labels nobody corrupted and found alpha 1.0 LOSES at every correction: label_smooth best at 0.25, oof_smooth and gp_smooth best at 0.5, downweight best at a 4-to-1 row weight ratio. The two experiments ask different questions -- share of an injected gap recovered, against held-out spearman on real labels -- and which one sets the default is an open decision.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 336 per training fold
loops.changed: the fold's homology groups are handed to the detector that decides which labels are suspect, instead of being withheld
loops.before: 0.2845 detection average precision on held-out fold 0 and 0.2056 on held-out fold 1, groups withheld
loops.after: 0.3322 detection average precision on held-out fold 0 and 0.2387 on held-out fold 1, groups given
loops.note: Two paired passes, one corruption draw, one dataset, one representation (esm2_cdr, which is what pick_noise_base_rep falls back to here). Giving the groups won both passes, by 0.0477 and by 0.0331 average precision, so the gain is larger than the difference between the two gains. Cross-checked by n20's own run the same night, which computed the same score with the groups withheld and wrote 0.2450 average precision averaged over its 2 passes at 30 corrupted of 336 training antibodies, against 0.2451 for the mean of the two withheld readings here. What it does not settle: whether the recipe the search then picks, or the held-out spearman, moves at all. n20's first result file, written that night, came back with its search scoring ONE candidate per fold, so the recipe could not move whatever the flag list said.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 per training fold, esm2_cdr, random forest, spearman, 3 scaffold-grouped folds
loops.changed: the scale the four score-proportional corrections read a suspicion score on, from the raw score the correction min-max rescales itself to the molecule's position in the ordering
loops.before: over the 24 readings the two runs share for those four corrections, the cleaned model beat the uncleaned one on 24 of 72 folds; gp_smooth averaged -0.0093 spearman over its 6 settings
loops.after: 27 of 72 folds; gp_smooth averaged -0.0267 spearman over the same 6 settings
loops.note: Mixed and mostly worse, so the knob was removed rather than left beside the raw score. downweight improved, from winning 7 of 18 folds to 10 of 18; gp_smooth got clearly worse; label_smooth and oof_smooth did not move. loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 per training fold, esm2_cdr, random forest, spearman, 3 scaffold-grouped folds
loops.changed: nothing in the file: the existing strength grid was read out per correction, to settle whether moving a label all the way beats moving it a quarter of the way
loops.before: the uncleaned random forest, 0.4590 spearman
loops.after: the strongest setting loses at every correction. label_smooth is best at alpha 0.25, 0.4492 spearman against 0.4185 at alpha 1.0. oof_smooth is best at alpha 0.5, 0.4651 against 0.4512 at alpha 1.0. gp_smooth is best at alpha 0.5, 0.4726 against 0.4705 at alpha 1.0. downweight is best at a 4-to-1 row weight ratio, 0.4823 against 0.4687 at 10-to-1
loops.note: The grid does not need extending above alpha 1.0; it may need extending below 0.25 for label_smooth. Only one setting of the 44 scored won every fold: gp_smooth at alpha 1.0 with the cross_val detector, 3 of 3 folds, 0.4590 to 0.4705 spearman. Two cautions. Both hybrid spaces were absent -- every stored search on disk is behind the distance_metric column commit 9c6f7d7 added, so this is the base representation alone. And the uncleaned score here is 0.4590 spearman where the earlier n18 entry on this dataset reads 0.5985, because pick_noise_base_rep has no ecfp4, pdv or blosum on an antibody set and falls back to esm2_cdr alphabetically, while the 0.5985 runs elsewhere in this ledger name saprot.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 in fold 0's training block, saprot, 1280 features
loops.changed: weighted the Gaussian process's kernel inputs by each feature's lightgbm gain, which is what cut a Gaussian process's error by 29 percent in n21
loops.before: the posterior mean gp_smooth aims every label at spans 1.6899 label units across the 448 molecules and rank-correlates with the labels it was fitted on at -0.0234 spearman
loops.after: the same 1.6899 label units and the same -0.0234 spearman; the two posterior means differ by 0.00000000 label units, bit-identical
loops.note: THE WEIGHTING IS NOT THE FINDING. It reached the kernel and it was drastic -- lightgbm gives gain to only 361 of saprot's 1280 features, so 919 columns were multiplied by zero and both guards in GaussianProcessEstimator passed. Nothing changed because the process is not reading its inputs. Counted directly: the 448 molecules receive 3 DISTINCT posterior-mean values, 64.0567, 65.7113 and 65.7467 label units, and each is exactly the mean label of the inner fold that molecule was held out of -- inner fold 0 trains on 298 molecules whose mean label is 64.0567 and every molecule it held out received 64.0567. The fitted noise level is 22.7930 label units against a fitted-label standard deviation of 22.8228, so the process assigns all of the variance to noise and its posterior mean is its prior mean. So gp_smooth does not move a label toward what a Gaussian process predicts for that molecule, which is what n07's docstring says it does; it moves every label toward the mean label of its inner fold. It is shrinkage toward the mean under a model's name. This is one representation at 1280 features over 448 molecules, which is the regime where an isotropic RBF kernel flattens because every pair of molecules is nearly the same distance apart; whether a narrower feature set revives it is not measured.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, saprot, 448 in the training fold, 1280 features, injected level 2.0, one molecule in ten corrupted
loops.changed: the gaussian process that gp_smooth corrects toward had its kernel inputs multiplied by feature importance, instead of left unweighted
loops.before: share of the 0.2538 spearman clean-to-corrupted gap recovered, unweighted: 28.4% moving a label a quarter of the way, 47.5% all the way, 41.3% by rank, 31.1% replacing outright
loops.after: identical to four decimal places at all four shapes: 28.4%, 47.5%, 41.3%, 31.1%
loops.note: ⛔ NOT a null result about weighting. The gaussian process is DEGENERATE at the width n07 fits it at, so there is nothing for a weighting to change. Fitted on all 1280 features it returned 3 distinct posterior-mean values across 448 training molecules -- one constant per inner fold, nothing read from the features -- and the same at the 361 features lightgbm gives any gain. It starts fitting between 361 features and 200: at 200 it returns 226 distinct values and beats the corrupted labels by 0.3303 spearman against -0.0441 at 1280. This is the likely reason gp_smooth ranked second from bottom of the seven corrections at 13.4% -- it was smoothing toward a constant. At 200 features the weighting LOSES, 0.2709 against 0.3303 spearman, one fold only. The width has to be fixed before the weighting question can be asked, and the 29% gain measured for the similarity work is not contradicted by this -- it was measured where the process was actually fitting.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 336 per training fold
loops.changed: whether gaussian_process is counted as a source that predicts a molecule's noise from its features alone, which decides whether the result file marks it undefined under the default condition outlier_p10
loops.before: four of the five uncertainty sources marked undefined under outlier_p10, one of them scoring 0.3016 detection average precision against 0.0863 for a coin flip
loops.after: three of the five marked undefined; the source moved out scores that same 0.3016 detection average precision against 0.0863 for a coin flip, the highest of the five measured
loops.note: Its score is the posterior spread plus the out-of-fold residual (noise_estimation.py:911-916), and the residual reads the molecule's own label, so it is not a prediction from features. One outer fold of two, one draw, two inner folds. It does not settle whether the cleaning that follows the ranking wins folds.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 336 per training fold
loops.changed: the injected noise condition, from the default outlier_p10 to censoring, to give the feature-based sources a condition whose corrupted molecules are chosen by something the features encode
loops.before: under outlier_p10 at level 0.5, with 29 of the 336 training molecules moved and a coin flip at 0.0863, detection average precision was 0.3016 for gaussian_process, 0.2664 for activity_cliff_aware and 0.0878 for heteroscedastic_nn
loops.after: under censoring at level 0.25, with 79 and 86 of the 336 training molecules moved on the two folds and a coin flip at 0.2351 and 0.2560, detection average precision was 0.2663 and 0.2764 for gaussian_process, 0.1947 and 0.2776 for heteroscedastic_nn, and 0.1881 and 0.2340 for activity_cliff_aware
loops.note: Every source sits at the coin flip under censoring and two of the three sit below it, so the default stays outlier_p10. Clipping every label above a cut-point pulls the top of the range together, so a clipped label is not far from its neighbours. grouped_wider, the only entry in NOISE_KEYED_TO_STRUCTURE, could not be measured at all: it needs one scaffold-group id per molecule and an antibody set loads no SMILES. ngboost and hetero_gp had not finished under either condition when this was written.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 336 per training fold
loops.changed: what n23 does when asked for a grouped condition on a dataset with no scaffold groups: it now stops before the first fold instead of injecting
loops.before: every one of the outer folds raised inside the injector, each wrote one row into _errors, and the run finished and saved a result file carrying 0 held-out scores
loops.after: the run stops with a message naming the 4 conditions in DETECTION_IS_DEFINED that need no scaffold groups, and writes no file
loops.note: Only reachable on a dataset that loads no SMILES. caco2 and herg_ki have them and are unaffected. The before number is a count of scores in the file, not a score.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 in fold 0's training block, saprot narrowed to its highest-gain features
loops.changed: weighted the Gaussian process's kernel inputs by each feature's lightgbm gain, at the three widths where the process actually fits rather than at the full 1280 where it returns a constant
loops.before: unweighted, the target's agreement with the clean labels is 0.3303 spearman at 200 features, 0.2473 at 50 and 0.4360 at 5; its distance from the clean label of the molecules the injector gave the wide error is 10.4195, 10.4816 and 9.2341 label units
loops.after: weighted, 0.2709 spearman at 200 features, 0.2182 at 50 and 0.4463 at 5; the distances are 10.7427, 10.8975 and 9.4700 label units
loops.note: This is the weighting question asked where it can be answered. The earlier reading at the full 1280 features said nothing about weighting: the posterior mean there is one constant per inner fold, so weighting the inputs of a constant cannot move it, and the numbers came back bit-identical. NOT A CLEAN NEGATIVE. Weighting loses on agreement with the clean labels at 2 of the 3 live widths and WINS at 5 features, 0.4463 against 0.4360 spearman. It loses on the distance to the damaged molecules' clean labels at 3 of 3, by 0.32, 0.42 and 0.24 label units. So the two readings disagree at 5 features and agree everywhere else. One fold and one noise draw behind each, so this is a direction. The n21 result it was testing -- weighting an RBF kernel's inputs cutting a Gaussian process's error by 29 percent on a similarity task -- does not transfer here on this evidence. NOT APPLIED: nothing in n07 passes feature_weights, and nothing now will.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 per training fold, 3 outer folds, 1 corruption draw, condition outlier_p10
loops.changed: n12 now refuses to write a recovery percentage when the clean-to-noisy gap it divides by is under 2 percent of the clean score, which is the floor n06, n07, n11 and n21 already apply; the gap was measured at five injected levels before any recovery number was read
loops.before: n12's only guard was a gap larger than 1e-10. In its result file of 2026-09-20, measured in the esm2_cdr representation, the random forest's clean-to-noisy gap under outlier_p10 at level 0.5 was 0.008551 spearman against a clean score of 0.458964 -- 1.86 percent of it -- and lightgbm's was 0.048543 against a clean score of 0.426777 -- 11.37 percent. Of the 192 recovery readings in that file, 104 fell outside 0 to 100 percent: 68 below 0 and 36 above 100. The random forest's 96 readings ran from -615.6 to +578.0 percent and lightgbm's 96 ran from -33.9 to +149.3 percent
loops.after: the 2 percent floor refuses all 96 of the random forest's readings in that file and keeps all 96 of lightgbm's, which removes 79 of the 104 readings outside 0 to 100 percent and leaves 25. Measured today in the onehot representation, which pick_noise_base_rep now returns for this dataset, the random forest's gap at level 0.5 is 0.062572 spearman against a clean score of 0.406820 -- 15.38 percent of it -- and lightgbm's is 0.027025 spearman against a clean score of 0.375947 -- 7.19 percent. Both clear the floor, so no reading at level 0.5 in onehot is refused. At level 1.5 the random forest reads 0.128583 spearman (31.61 percent of its clean score) and lightgbm 0.120551 (32.07 percent)
loops.note: THE DOSE WAS NOT RAISED and the level was not changed. The unreadable figure was the esm2_cdr control arm, not the level: the same condition and the same level in onehot gives the random forest a gap 7.3 times larger as a share of its clean score. The two sets of numbers are NOT comparable as measurements of anything but the gap, because the control arm changed. 40 of the 448 training molecules had their label moved at every level -- outlier_p10 moves a fixed share and the level sets how far, so the count does not rise with the level. The random forest's gap is not monotonic in the level: 31.61 percent at 1.5 then 28.79 percent at 2.0. One draw and three folds behind each number, and the three folds' clean random forest scores were 0.590534, 0.268802 and 0.361124 spearman, so the fold spread is wider than most of the gaps. Nothing here measures whether a better detector repairs better.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, condition outlier_p10 at level 0.5, from the result file of 2026-09-20 plus a synthetic check of the new code
loops.changed: n12 records which of its conditions are a second copy of another condition rather than a measurement of their own, and reuses the importance array instead of computing it a second time
loops.before: each hybrid space carries an _imp_base condition weighted by the recipe's own importance method and an _imp_own condition weighted by the method the sweep is on. Both recipes ranked their features by lightgbm_gain, so on the lightgbm_gain half of the sweep hybrid_imp_base and hybrid_imp_own agreed to 1e-12 in 6 of 6 detection average precision readings, and hybrid_similarity_imp_base and hybrid_similarity_imp_own agreed in 6 of 6. 2 of the 16 importance-method-by-condition cells were duplicates and nothing in the result file said so
loops.after: those 2 cells are named in results['duplicate_conditions'] with the condition each copies and why, and each one saves one importance computation on the hybrid matrix per fold and per space. On the treeshap half the same two pairs agreed in 0 of 6 readings and nothing is recorded, which is what a second measurement looks like
loops.note: The reused array makes the duplicate condition bit-identical to the one it copies, checked on a 120-row synthetic matrix: identical under lightgbm_gain, different under treeshap. The condition keeps its own name in the result file, so nothing that reads it breaks. NOT RE-MEASURED on the real dataset -- flab_thermo_tresanco's stored search is missing the distance_metric column commit 9c6f7d7 added, so n12.run cannot open the pool and cannot build a hybrid space at all until that store is rebuilt.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 in fold 0's training block, saprot, 1280 features, injected level 2.0 of the clean label standard deviation, one molecule in ten given the wide error
loops.changed: the RBF kernel's length scale starts at the median distance between the training molecules it is fitted on, instead of at 1.0, in GaussianProcessEstimator.estimate (src/kirby/utils/noise_estimation.py)
loops.before: the posterior mean gp_smooth aims every label at took 3 distinct values across the 448 molecules, rank-correlated with the CLEAN labels at -0.0441 spearman, and sat 11.0137 label units from the clean label of the 39 molecules the injector gave the wide error
loops.after: 358 distinct values across the same 448 molecules, 0.5630 spearman against the clean labels, and 9.5756 label units from those 39 molecules' clean labels
loops.note: THE MECHANISM, not a tuning choice. An RBF kernel is exp(-d^2 / 2l^2). Two standardised molecules described by saprot's 1280 features sit about sqrt(2 * 1280) = 50.6 apart, so at a length scale of 1.0 every off-diagonal entry of the kernel matrix underflows, the matrix is the identity and the marginal likelihood is flat in the length scale. Recorded per inner fold: the three fitted length scales came back 1.01, 1.00 and 1.01, having never left the start, and the white-noise level pinned at 1.0, its own upper bound. After the change they are 61.87, 54.26 and 41.85 with noise levels 0.8884, 0.8328 and 0.8446. sklearn's n_restarts_optimizer=3 does not rescue it because each restart is sampled log-uniformly across the length-scale bounds, which were (1e-5, 1e5) -- ten orders of magnitude -- so a restart almost never lands near the data's own distance; the bounds are now a factor of 100 either side of the start. NARROWING THE FEATURE SET IS NO LONGER NEEDED: at 1280 features the fixed start reaches 0.5630 spearman against the clean labels, beating every narrowed width measured against the broken start (0.3303 at 200 features, 0.2473 at 50, 0.4360 at 5). At 200 features the fixed start reaches 0.6014, so width still buys something, and at 5 features the two starts agree to four decimals (0.4360 both) because a median distance of about 3 and a start of 1.0 are close enough. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: one fold, one noise draw, one dataset, one representation. This is the TARGET's quality, not a recovery figure -- what it does to the share of the clean-to-corrupted gap gp_smooth puts back is the next measurement. It also changes every other caller of GaussianProcessEstimator: n07's own 'gaussian_process' detector and n11's gp target and detector. Neither was re-measured here. The same median heuristic was already in this file's heteroscedastic Gaussian process (torch.cdist(...).median()).

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 448 per training fold, 3 outer folds, 1 corruption draw, condition outlier_p10 at level 0.5, 40 of the 448 training molecules moved
loops.changed: cut the base representation to its highest-importance features by a hard budget, to ask whether n12's hybrid advantage is about mixing representations or only about how many features the distance is computed over
loops.before: the full 5600-feature onehot representation, unweighted, reads 0.1937 mean detection average precision over the 12 rows of importance scorer by neighbour count; weighting it by importance to the power 0.5, which is what n12 does, reads 0.2176 and beats it in 12 of 12 rows
loops.after: a hard cut of that same representation to its top 50 features, with no weighting and no second representation, reads 0.2207 mean detection average precision and beats the full-width unweighted space in 10 of 12 rows; at top 200 it reads 0.2039 in 9 of 12 rows and at top 500 0.1946 in 6 of 12
loops.note: NOT APPLIED to n12: nothing in the file was changed by this and the conditions are unchanged. What it settles is that the 6-of-6 result in n12's result file of 2026-09-20 -- the unweighted hybrid beating the unweighted base representation in 6 of 6 readings under both scorers -- does not need a mix of representations to appear. Narrowing ONE representation to the hybrid's own budget of 50 features reproduces it. What it does NOT settle: whether narrowing beats weighting. 0.2207 against 0.2176 mean average precision is 0.0031 apart on 3 folds and one draw, and the three folds' clean random forest scores on this dataset were 0.590534, 0.268802 and 0.361124 spearman, so the fold spread is far wider than that. It also does not measure the hybrid itself -- flab_thermo_tresanco's stored search is missing the distance_metric column commit 9c6f7d7 added, so no hybrid space could be built tonight.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, plus a 300-row 4000-feature synthetic matrix for the exactness check
loops.changed: a weighted space now drops the features the importance scorer gave zero, whose column is exact zeros, before the neighbour search runs
loops.before: the estimators searched a space 5600 features wide in every weighted condition. Of onehot's 5600 features, lightgbm_gain scored 181, 169 and 164 above zero on the three folds and treeshap 1086 and 1117, so between 4483 and 5436 of the columns were zeros. Three neighbour searches over the synthetic matrix's full 4000 features took 26.52 seconds
loops.after: the space is as wide as the live features, so between 164 and 1117 features on this dataset. Three neighbour searches over that matrix's 150 live features took 0.79 seconds. Across all four distance metrics the suite sweeps, four exponents, both estimators and two neighbour counts, 64 of 64 comparisons returned bit-identical suspicion scores
loops.note: No number n12 produces changes: manhattan, euclidean and minkowski_p0.5 all sum a per-feature term that is zero when both values are zero, and cosine's dot product and both norms gain zero from such a column, and there is no per-row centring in that list. At exponent 0.0 numpy gives 0 ** 0 == 1, so nothing is dropped and the control that the weighted space equals the unweighted one still holds. The timing was taken on a synthetic matrix; the machine was at a one-minute load of over 400 all evening, so the real-run saving was not timed.

loops.dataset: herg_ic50, 12,008 measurement rows over 9,802 molecules, ecfp4 alone, 3 scaffold-grouped folds, 1 draw of which measurement trains, rf as the only downstream model. 1,218 of the 9,802 molecules carry more than one measurement and 405 carry three or more, so 405 molecules can be graded and about 129 of them are held out per fold.
loops.changed: the share of training molecules every removing arm takes out, from 0.10 to 0.01. At 0.10 a training fold of about 6,535 molecules is asked for 653; at 0.01 it is asked for 65. About 824 molecules in a training fold have a repeat measurement at all, and only 640 molecules in the whole dataset disagree across their repeats, so at 653 the ceiling necessarily also removes molecules whose repeats agree exactly.
loops.before: distance from floor_measured to ceiling at 0.10: -0.0167 rmse in log units of pIC50. Negative means the ceiling LOST to a random pick from the same molecules -- ceiling 0.8102 rmse against floor_measured 0.7936 -- so n17 reported no removal position at all.
loops.after: distance from floor_measured to ceiling at 0.01: +0.0071 rmse in log units of pIC50. Ceiling 0.7471 rmse against floor_measured 0.7542, so a distance exists and n17 reported a removal position for the first time.
loops.note: The file's default share is still 0.10 and was not moved: which share ships is the owner's to set, and this is the number to set it against. What the sign change does NOT buy is a removal result. At both shares no_cleaning is the best arm on every one of the 3 folds -- 0.7399 rmse against drop 0.7629 and repair 0.7653 at 0.01, and against drop 0.8161 and repair 0.8279 at 0.10. Both detector arms sit BELOW their own floor at 0.01, at -0.0143 and -0.0167 rmse, which the read-out prints as -200% and -234% of the way from floor to ceiling: neighbor_residual at k=10 in ecfp4 picks worse than a random pick from the same molecules. One draw only, so there is no spread over which measurement became the training label. No hybrid space ran: only ecfp4 is cached for herg_ic50 on this machine and a hybrid needs at least two representations, so both the predictive and the similarity hybrid spaces were refused before any search started and every number above is in ecfp4 alone. Each run cost about 6,100 seconds of wall clock at 8 to 11 percent of one core.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 336 in fold 0's training block, esm2_cdr at 1280 features, outlier_p10 at level 0.5, draw 0, two inner folds
loops.changed: ngboost's boosting schedule, from 500 stages at learning rate 0.01 to 50 stages at learning rate 0.1, holding the product of the two at 5
loops.before: 219.6 CPU-seconds for one uncertainty estimate, and 0.1500 average precision at ranking the 29 of the 336 training molecules whose label moved, against 0.0863 average precision for a coin flip
loops.after: 21.9 CPU-seconds for the same estimate, and 0.1313 average precision at ranking the same 29 of 336 training molecules, against the same 0.0863 for a coin flip
loops.note: THE POINT IS THE COST, NOT THE DETECTION. ngboost had never returned a number to n23 at all: the run on 2026-09-21 was abandoned after 18 minutes with no reading. One boosting stage costs 0.24 CPU-seconds at 1280 features and 1.00 CPU-seconds at 5600, measured directly on 168 training rows, and n23 gives the estimator 2 inner folds -- so at 500 stages one estimate is 240 CPU-seconds at 1280 features and 1000 at 5600. pick_noise_base_rep now returns onehot on an antibody set, which is 5600 features wide, and n23's headline needs 6 estimates (3 outer folds at each of 2 injected levels), so the old schedule was 100 CPU-minutes of one source. NEITHER AVERAGE PRECISION IS EVIDENCE ABOUT NGBOOST'S DETECTION: outlier_p10 picks the molecules it corrupts at random with no reference to the features, and ngboost predicts a molecule's spread FROM its features, so n23 already marks it undefined under this condition. On the same fold gaussian_process scores 0.3016 and activity_cliff_aware 0.2664. DEVIATES FROM THE SHARED SPEC, which it did not match before either: qsar_qm_models/models/model_defaults.py version 1.7.0 carries n_estimators 500 for ngboost together with early_stopping_rounds 50 and use_best_iteration true, so 500 is a CAP a validation curve is meant to stop short of; NGBoostEstimator reads neither stopping key and fitted all 500 stages every time. Reading that curve would need a validation split carved inside each inner fold, and _oof_apply hands fold_fn no scaffold ids, so an ungrouped carve would put a molecule's own family on both sides of it. n11 and n13 also list ngboost as an optional estimator and both get the shorter schedule; neither has a recorded ngboost reading to compare against.

loops.dataset: flab_thermo_tresanco, 672 antibodies, 336 in fold 0's training block, esm2_cdr at 1280 features, outlier_p10 at level 0.5, draw 0, two inner folds
loops.changed: nothing in the file: hetero_gp was run on one outer fold on its own, instead of behind every arm and every fold of a full n23 run
loops.before: no number at all -- hetero_gp is the one of the five uncertainty sources that had never been reached, and the two n23 runs that asked for it were abandoned first
loops.after: 0.0850 average precision at ranking the 29 of the 336 training molecules whose label moved, against 0.0863 average precision for a coin flip, in 41.7 CPU-seconds, giving 278 distinct scores over the 336 molecules
loops.note: hetero_gp is NOT expensive and it was never the reason a run did not finish: 41.7 CPU-seconds against 487.5 wall-seconds, because the machine was carrying 91 python processes and this one held 8.6 percent of a core. It sits AT the coin flip, which is what the file predicts for it: it predicts a molecule's noise from its features and outlier_p10 picks the molecules it corrupts at random, so n23 marks it undefined under this condition and a chance-level reading is the condition rather than the method. The 278 distinct scores say the network is not flat, so this is not the failure the estimator's own note describes. All five sources now have a reading on this one fold: gaussian_process 0.3016, activity_cliff_aware 0.2664, ngboost 0.1313, heteroscedastic_nn 0.0878, hetero_gp 0.0850, coin flip 0.0863. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE: this is detection on one fold. Whether the cleaning that follows any of these rankings wins a held-out fold is a separate run.
